Subject: Hosted API — looking for an annual reserve + pricing tiers overview

Hi Irene,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the latency profile looked promising. We're starting internal planning for next fiscal year and want to understand how Redwood's hosted API could map to a predictable cost model. Specifically:

- We prefer a usage-based model but want to reserve capacity (to lock pricing and get volume discounts).
- Can you outline a Starter / Growth / Enterprise reserve (annual) with price per token at each slab, and a simple true-up/credit model if we under- or over-use?
- Any guidance on burst capacity and how carry-forward of unused tokens works?

We're targeting a Monday (2027-02-14) internal review so a short, tabular proposal would be helpful.

Best,
Sophia Ramirez
Head of AI Platform, Acme Payroll
[sophia@acmepay.com]

Hi Sophia — appreciate the note and the timeline. Attaching a first pass that maps to the Starter/Growth/Enterprise buckets and includes a short FAQ on carry-forward, true-ups, and burst. High level summary here inline: 

Starter (annual reserve ~ 1M tokens/month average across year)
- Per-token base: $0.000045/token
- Minimum annual commit: $540/month equivalent billed monthly (pre-commit discount applied as credits)
- Carry-forward: up to 10% of monthly allocation can roll into next quarter (not year)
- True-up: quarterly true-up; if usage exceeds reserved tokens, overage billed monthly at the next tier's per-token rate with a 5% buffer discount for first two quarters of term

Growth (6M tokens/month average)
- Per-token base: $0.000035/token
- Flexible buffer: +20% burst at reserved price for short spikes (subject to capacity)
- Carry-forward: up to 20% of quarterly unused tokens applied to next quarter
- True-up: annual true-up with pro-rata credits for underspend

Enterprise (25M+ tokens/month average)
- Per-token base: $0.000022/token
- Custom SLA and dedicated routing options; dedicated capacity available under Redwood Dedicated addendum
- Carry-forward: negotiated (typical 6–12 month smoothing window)
- True-up: annual true-up with laddered credits and option for pre-paid top-ups

Notes on pricing mechanics and why tiers: the platform optimizes unit cost via batching/kv-cache effectiveness and quantization profiles. We model expected per-token cost vs observed sequence length distribution to pick the right slab. The attached spreadsheet has worked examples (monthly burn schedules + sample True-up math).

Attachments: 20270201-token-reserve-proposal.xlsx (summary table + worked examples)

If it's useful, Marissa can formalize this into a one-pager with a small variance window and a sample contract clause for carry-forward / smoothing. Vivek can run a quick estimate against your Q1 prompt set to propose a recommended tier.

Best,
Irene Choi

Hi Sophia — looping in with a short pricing play and an optional smoothing/credit mechanic that legal likes.

Pricing play (short):
- Starter: 12-month term; 5% discount if paid upfront; carry-forward capped at 10%/quarter; overages billed at Growth per-token rate + 3% admin
- Growth: 12-month term with a 10% uplift credit applied if you commit to 18 months; quarterly reporting and a 20% short-term burst window at reserved price for first 6 months
- Enterprise: flexible multi-year; floor usage guarantees reduce rate by additional 2–4% depending on term and payment cadence

Smoothing proposal: create a "smoothing credit" pool representing up to 8% of annual committed tokens. Under-spend flows into the pool and offsets overages for a 12-month window; pool administration fee only if you request monthly split billing. This helps with seasonality (e.g., open enrollment spikes).

Irene — I drafted a sample clause and marked the cells in the spreadsheet for the legal-friendly language. Sophia — if you can share a rough monthly usage cadence, I can generate Starter/Growth/Enterprise price rows with example numbers and a 12-month smoothing projection.

- Marissa
Account Director, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: RDW-Acme-SLA-deltas.pdf (application/pdf)]

1) Can you show a concrete example for each tier with baseline numbers? e.g., Starter = 12M tokens/year, Growth = 72M tokens/year, Enterprise = 300M tokens/year — and the effective $/token after smoothing and credits?
2) How does the smoothing pool affect year 2 renewals? Do unused credits expire?
3) For Enterprise, can you confirm whether dedicated capacity pricing is additive or replaces hosted per-token rate?

Also — our procurement team prefers simple clauses for true-ups (quarterly/notified) and wants a limit on retroactive adjustments (max 6 months).

Onboarding: we plan to pilot in March if we can get a contract by mid-February.

Ben / Sophia — thanks for the clear asks. Quick summary and next steps below (also updated the Drive folder).

Concrete worked examples (effective $/token assumes expected batching/sequence distribution from your sample prompts — Vivek ran the estimate):
- Starter: 12M tokens/year (avg 1M/month) — sticker: $0.000045/token; after 10% smoothing applied conservatively: effective $0.0000405/token; annual cost: $540 (monthly equivalent) x 12 = $6,480 with option for 5% prepaid discount down to ~$6,156
- Growth: 72M tokens/year — sticker: $0.000035/token; smoothing pool applied (8%): effective $0.0000322/token; annual cost: ~$2,314
- Enterprise: 360M tokens/year — sticker: $0.000022/token; with negotiated smoothing + multi-year floor: effective $0.000020/token; annual cost: ~$7,200 (example — final depends on exact commit and routing choices)

Smoothing and expiry: smoothing pool tokens expire after 12 months; unused tokens at contract end convert to pro-rata credits against invoice finalization (no cash refunds). We can limit retroactive adjustments to 6 months as you requested.

Dedicated capacity note: dedicated capacity is priced as an add-on (monthly reserved capacity fee) that replaces some hosted routing for guaranteed latency; the per-token hosted rate is adjusted down when you add Dedicated because overall unit cost assumptions change — we can show a blended example in the contract appendix.

Next steps:
1) Marissa to prepare a one-page commercial term sheet with the three worked examples (Starter/Growth/Enterprise) + sample smoothing clause (EOD 2027-02-11).
2) Acme to share a one-page monthly cadence (expected seasonality) — Marissa will run numbers and Vivek will validate latency/cost assumptions.
3) Targeting signature on a 12-month Starter PO by 2027-02-18 to keep March pilot timeline.

I'll drop a calendar invite for a 30-min pricing alignment tomorrow. If you prefer, we can also produce a short legal-friendly amendment to an SOW that captures the smoothing pool mechanics.

Thanks — talk soon,
